frames.narration: Alice opens the shop for the first time. Nothing is cached anywhere, so GET /app.3f9a.js goes all the way to the origin. The origin answers 200 with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable and ETag: "a1". The CDN and the browser both store it.

Three days later she returns. The stored copy has age 3 days, far below the 31536000 s lifetime, so the browser reuses it without sending any request: 0 bytes, no round trip. A normal reload does not even revalidate it, because of immutable.

The HTML page is sent with Cache-Control: no-cache and ETag: "h1". no-cache does not mean do not store: the browser keeps the copy but must ask before every reuse. It sends If-None-Match: "h1" and the origin replies 304 Not Modified, about 300 bytes and no body.

A deploy changes the page. The next visit sends If-None-Match: "h1" but the origin now has ETag "h2", so it answers 200 with the new HTML. The new HTML names /app.7be2.js, a URL nobody has cached, so that is a fresh miss. Alice gets the new code immediately and the old file is untouched.

The API (/api/products) is sent with max-age=60. Bob fetched it 50 s ago, so the CDN holds a copy with Age: 50. Alice's browser stores it with that age, so it has only 60 - 50 = 10 s of freshness left. The Age header makes freshness add up across layers instead of restarting at each cache.

A different API is sent with max-age=30, stale-while-revalidate=120. At age 45 s it is stale, but inside the 120 s window. The browser answers instantly from the stale copy and revalidates in the background. The user waits 0 ms and the next request has the new data.

The profile (/api/me) is personal. It is sent with Cache-Control: private, no-cache, so the CDN must not store it: it just passes the request through. Only Alice's own browser keeps a copy, and it revalidates every time. Without private, the CDN could hand Alice's profile to Bob.

The classic mistake: the HTML was once sent with max-age=86400. After the next deploy the origin has h3, but Alice's browser (and the CDN) still treat the stored page as fresh for up to 24 hours. Nobody asks the origin, so the fix cannot reach her. The only escapes are waiting, a hard reload, or purging the CDN, and the browser copies cannot be purged.
